RQ1.rationale: The paper substantially addresses general CubeSat/nanosatellite mission modeling through a reusable logical reference model, stakeholders, lifecycle coverage, mission enterprise decomposition, and power subsystem/parametric elements; EPS detail remains subsystem-level rather than component-specific.

RQ2.rationale: It claims reuse, consistency, reduced systems-engineering burden, integration with simulations, and power-related trade studies, but does not provide direct EPS reliability/reproducibility/integrability metrics.

RQ3.rationale: Verification and testing appear at system level through MBSE definition, tester stakeholder, Cal Poly testing requirements, and mission-specific validation/verification strategies, but no EPS-specific pre-physical verification procedure is described.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper summarizes earlier SSWG phases and prior RAX/power trade-study work as background; those summaries are treated only as evidence reported in this paper. The corpus metadata author list differs from the visible markdown title block, so the visible paper authors are used here.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: SysML/OOSEM is the core, but the model is explicitly positioned as a central repository that integrates discipline-specific models/simulations, COTS simulation tools, distribution mechanisms, and component libraries.
tailoring_rationale: Most CubeSat groups are first-time developers with limited systems-engineering resources.
Low cost and short lifecycles make a reusable starting model and checklist valuable.
A logical architecture avoids over-constraining mission-specific physical designs.
The specific architecture methodology is less important than providing a foundation for users to create physical architectures.
Regulatory timelines must be understood early because CubeSat projects are international but licensing/regulation is national.

practical_implementation_pathway.rationale: The paper outlines stakeholder capture, logical architecture, mission-specific model creation, distribution, and trade-study workflow, but does not provide a completed step-by-step adoption playbook or validated example in this phase.

toolchain_fragmentation_interoperability.rationale: COTS simulation interfaces and distribution mechanisms such as XMI/OpenMBEE/Teamcenter are identified, but detailed interoperability implementation and round-trip evidence are absent.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: The motivation explicitly targets small, first-time, low-budget CubeSat teams and proposes a reusable checklist/reference model, but effort savings are not measured.

governance_project_deliverables_roi_valu.rationale: The paper discusses licensing, copyright, distribution, stakeholder measures, and model-derived trade indicators, but lacks quantified ROI or formal deliverable/review linkage.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: Low-cost, short-lifecycle, worldwide CubeSat development and distributed SSWG teleconferencing are mentioned, but agile/rapid-iteration methods are not developed.

RQ1: A CubeSat mission can be modeled generically as a SysML/OOSEM logical reference architecture covering stakeholders, lifecycle, operations phases, mission enterprise components, and space/ground subsystems.
The Power subsystem appears as a logical space subsystem, and the minimum reference-model content includes subsystem-level power and weight parametrics.
The approach handles limited behavioral knowledge by starting with logical architecture, stakeholder measures, and trade parameters before mission-specific physical behavior is developed.
RQ2: Claimed benefits include reuse/adaptability, reduced systems-engineering burden, checklist support, uniformity, consistency, integration of simulations, and concept trade-study support.
Power/EPS-adjacent outcomes are limited to prior system power modeling and energy trade studies; no EPS reliability or quantified integrability/reproducibility outcomes are shown.
Evidence strength is mostly weak to moderate because current-phase benefits are asserted or summarized from prior demonstrations without baseline comparisons.
RQ3: Verification is integrated only generically: MBSE supports verification/validation, tester stakeholders are defined, Cal Poly testing requirements are modeled, and mission-specific models include V&V strategies.
No EPS-specific requirement-to-verification case, executable verification procedure, or physical/integration test result is reported.
Pre-physical development evidence is strongest for concept trade studies and requirements modeling, not for EPS verification.

extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: EPS is represented only at logical power-subsystem, power-parametric, and prior energy-trade level; no detailed EPS architecture is modeled.
No reliability, reproducibility, integrability, cost, or schedule metrics are provided.
No public reusable model file or validated toolchain-exchange evidence is included.
Verification and testing are system-level concepts; no EPS-specific pre-physical verification workflow is demonstrated.
The paper's current-phase reference model has not yet been validated through the planned example mission-specific model.
